text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London drifted back in lackluster trade, ending the session mixed. August lost 30 cents to close at $322.90 per tonne, while October added 10 cents to close at $317.40 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended slightly higher with players focused on the nearby switch. The July/October spread narrowed to 5 points from 7 points on Tuesday. July added 2 points to close at 11.36 cents/lb, while October closed 5 points higher at 11.31 cents/lb. Despite today's gains, prices must be expected to ease gradually ahead of the expiry of July, on June 30.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong imported 20,166 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in April 1997, down from 23,040 tonnes imported the previous month but up from the 19,204 tonnes imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 91,765 tonnes, nearly 6 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. The main supplier of white sugar in January/April 1997 was South Korea with 58,913 tonnes, up from 37,634 tonnes the same period in 1996. Another leading supplier was the United Kingdom with 11,989 tonnes against 7,642 tonnes in January/April 1996.

The country exported 34,560 tonnes of sugar in January/April 1997, 30 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose to 80,533 tonnes from 67,970 tonnes the previous year.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 159,876 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in April 1997, 34 per cent more than was exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports in crop year 1996/97 (May/April) up to 5.368 million tonnes, 9 per cent less than was exported the previous year in spite of an increase in production of more than 7 per cent. This suggests, that there has been a noticeable build up in stocks in 1996/97 in spite of rising consumption.

The largest customer for raw sugar in 1996/97 were the United States with 235,367 tonnes, up from 172,502 tonnes the previous year. The main market for white sugar in 1996/97 was Nigeria with 555,685 tonnes, up from 421,609 tonnes the previous year. 131,900 tonnes of raw sugar (437,296 tonnes) and 272,449 tonnes (560,251 tonnes) of white sugar were shipped to Russia in 1996/97.

DENMARK - During the period from 9 to 15 June, temperatures ranged between 16 and 18 C. Rains were between 83 to 142 mm, below the average of 104-111 mm. Growth was said to be excellent. Beet diseases are insignificant and crop prospects are said to be normal to slightly above normal.
F.O. LICHT - Our third estimate of the world sugar balance 1996/97 will be released at 14.00 hrs central European time.

Syria has cancelled tenders to buy 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar and 13,000 tonnes of white sugar, a General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) official said. The sugar was for July and August delivery.

The European Union awarded 30,350 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 42.168 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on June 18. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to June 18 reached 2,249,575 tonnes, which compares to 2,387,448 tonnes last year.
